correctness.rationale: Every six-vertex length-five corner geodesic on L5 must have color profile (2,2,2) under a three-coloring. Comparing successive rung positions forces t_{j+1}=b_j and b_{j+1}=t_j and therefore t0=t2=t4, contradicting the length-four top-row geodesic. The constructed four-column stripe meets every geodesic of length <=5, treating mixed endpoints separately; the finite boundary cases have exact explicit colorings. Reproduced exhaustive small-case and pattern checks in verify_ladder.py. Proof applies to all finite and infinite ladders.

evidence: Unrestricted general-position coloring [3, Thm. 7.2] is at least five for n=7 and grows unboundedly, while this theorem asserts four for every n>=5.
For n<=6 the ladder diameter is at most five and prior [3] already settles relevant short instances.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The unrestricted condition implies the bounded condition, so the older values are an upper bound and coincide for small diameters. They cannot imply that four colors suffice on arbitrarily long ladders, and they are not stronger coverage of the n>=7 constant-plateau claim. Explicitly excludes short-case novelty.

value.rationale: The sharp all-order formula resolves one natural fixed-parameter width-two instance of the explicit product-coloring Question 6.2 in [1]. The local five-column geodesic balancing obstruction and period-four global optimal construction explain the threshold. The first strict separation from unrestricted general-position chromatic number at n=7 distinguishes the new structural regime rather than a routine repetition of a known short example.
